adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now loops over each destination calendar, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts). However, Office365 and Lark `createEvent` implementations ignore any per-credential selection and always take the first element: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then use `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` to build the target calendar URL/id (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts and packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). Since `CalendarManager.createEvent()` invokes `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` for every credential, those services will still write to the first destination calendar even when invoked for another host’s credential, which can target a calendarId not owned by that credential in collective multi-host scenarios.
